concepts.label: mctimings
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - no existing concept anywhere in the registry or extraction layer. Displays timing histograms/totals for Data-Service (memcached-binary-protocol) operations, sampled since the last stats reset or Data Service restart.

concepts.label: Memcached binary protocol
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - no existing concept for the raw memcached wire protocol anywhere in the registry or extraction layer, despite the corpus already having a protocol: namespace (protocol:dcp, protocol:grpc). This page is the first to name it directly and link to its external spec, listing GET/SET/ADD/REPLACE/INCREMENT/DECREMENT as example operation names defined by it.

concepts.label: port 11210 (KV / memcached)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - the non-secure connection port mctimings uses by default.

concepts.label: port 11207 (KV TLS)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already an extraction-layer candidate elsewhere in the corpus; this page states it directly as the TLS counterpart of port 11210 for secure mctimings connections.

concepts.label: cbstats
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - the page explicitly contrasts mctimings' timings with cbstats timings, stating the latter is less comprehensive.

concepts.label: cbstats-reset
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already an extraction-layer candidate elsewhere; this page names it as one of the two events that starts a new mctimings sampling period.

relations.subject: tool:mctimings
relations.evidence: Operations that can be explicitly specified include `GET` `SET`, `ADD`, `REPLACE`, `INCREMENT`, and `DECREMENT`. A comprehensive list can be found in the [memcached binary protocol reference](https://github.com/couchbase/memcached/blob/v4.5.1/docs/BinaryProtocol.md):

relations.subject: tool:mctimings
relations.evidence: For a non-secure connection, the port must be the memcached port, which is 11210.

relations.subject: tool:mctimings
relations.evidence: If a secure connection is to be made, the port must be specified as the TLS port, which is 11207; and the \--tls option must also be specified.

relations.subject: tool:mctimings
relations.evidence: Note that timings taken by `mctimings` are more comprehensive than those taken by [cbstats timings](cbstats/cbstats-timing.md); which, unlike `mctimings`, only measures the time spent on a request by a front-end worker thread; and does not include time spent fetching items from disk.

relations.subject: tool:mctimings
relations.evidence:
The sampling period, during which timings are taken, starts at whichever of the following points in time is the more recent:

* The last reset of Data-Service statistics by means of [cbstats-reset](#cli/cbstats/cbstats-reset.adoc).

notable_absence.finding: mctimings requires -u/-P administrator credentials but never names a role or privilege - the same pattern seen across most of this batch's tools (cbtransfer, cbworkloadgen, cbsummary, cbmigrate) apart from cbrecovery's explicit three-role citation. Notably, mctimings' -P option description is unusually detailed about password INPUT mechanics (CB_PASSWORD environment variable, stdin prompting via -S) while saying nothing about AUTHORIZATION - a page that is precise about one security dimension (how you supply a credential) and silent about another (what that credential must be able to do).

cross_component_finding: mctimings is the first page in the corpus to name the memcached binary protocol directly and link to its spec - a genuinely new piece of vocabulary this round's protocol: namespace (previously only protocol:dcp and protocol:grpc) had no occasion to name. It also draws a precise, stated contrast with the already-promoted tool:cbstats ('more comprehensive... does not include time spent fetching items from disk'), and depends on the already-extraction-layer tool:cbstats-reset-command for defining its own sampling window - tying this newly-discovered protocol vocabulary directly into the existing KV-statistics tool family (mcstat, cbstats) rather than leaving it isolated.
cross_product_finding: Like mcstat and mctestauth, mctimings connects directly to a node's raw KV/memcached port (11210 or the TLS port 11207) - connectivity Capella does not expose to customers. This is a Server (self-managed)-only diagnostic tool family; no page states the restriction outright, but the install-path table and direct-node-port model make it implicit across all three mc* pages in this batch.
